text:
Maria: Quick RFC follow-up — soft-boundary stitching + prefetch-pacing tradeoffs. Wanted to surface a few open questions before we lock the API.
Liam: sgtm, drop them here. main concern for me is handoff viscosity — how sticky are allocations across pool boundaries?
Sanjay: +1. If a tenant's pages are 'sticky' we can avoid churn, but it hurts multi-tenant fairness during bursts.
Neha: Can we quantify 'viscosity'? proposal: a moving-window metric = pages that survive >= N demote events / total pages touched. Helps tune demote aggressiveness.
Aj: That metric sounds useful. Also need to consider prefetch pacing impact on small-batch latency — prefetching too aggressively amplifies stall when many microbatches compete for staging bandwidth.
Maria: Right — tradeoffs: lower demote aggressiveness => lower eviction churn but higher memory pressure. More prefetch => fewer pagefaults but higher peak IO. Looking at three knobs: stitch threshold, prefetch credits, demote window.
Liam: For the stitching API, I still prefer explicit "soft-stitch" call we expose to the runtime: stitch(pool_a, pool_b, flags). Keeps operator semantics clear.
Sanjay: I worry explicit calls leak policy into callers. Could we keep soft-stitch as a hint in the allocation attributes instead? e.g., alloc(attrs = {bound: SOFT, affinity: pool_x})
Neha: We should support both: alloc hint + runtime-stitch operator for operators that do bulk moves during quieter windows.
Aj: Implementation detail: stitching must avoid touching live kernel objects in tight loops. Suggest streaming handoff: transfer descriptors in pages-of-N, yield to scheduler between chunks. Avoids 10ms GC pauses.
Maria: Good point. Also perf experiment idea: compare eager-stitch vs lazy-handoff over 1h workload with 20% bursty tenants. We need wiring in the telemetry to capture handoff latency and stall amplification.
OffloadBot: Deploy note: can run perf harness `rt-offload --workload microburst --stitch-mode lazy --prefetch 8` on canary.
Liam: About prefetch pacing: propose token-bucket per-tenant for staging IO. tokens generated at bandwidth rate. Prefetch consumes tokens. On token exhaustion, prefetches queue but requests still go through with fallback to smaller batches.
Sanjay: Token-bucket is nice and predictable. But ensure we have backpressure path to the request-level scheduler so user-facing latency SLOs are preserved.
Neha: On telemetry: emit metrics: `stitch_ops/sec`, `stitch_latency_p50/p95`, `prefetch_tokens_used`, `stall_amp_ratio` (requests delayed / baseline).
Aj: Small config snippet for experiments: ```
prefetch_policy:
  rate_bytes_per_sec: 200MB
  burst_tokens: 16
stitch:
  chunk_size_pages: 32
  yield_ms: 2
```
Maria: Can we add a graceful fallback: if stitch queue depth > X then switch to per-page demote to avoid long-running migrations?
Liam: Yes, fallback threshold should be tenant-aware. Large tenants get higher X. Also keep a global fence to prevent simultaneous heavy stitches across nodes.
Sanjay: One more interface thought: add `stitch_priority` to allocation hints. Runtime can escalate/delay based on global load.
Neha: Ops ask: a single knob to disable stitching entirely for latency-sensitive clusters — feature flag at the node level.
Maria: Action items: 1) Aj to prototype token-bucket prefetch and stitch streaming (perf harness + canary). 2) Neha to add telemetry fields and dashboards. 3) Liam + Sanjay to draft thin API: alloc-hint + runtime-stitch operator + node-level feature flag.
Aj: I'll start with the harness and the config above. Will post raw numbers once canary runs.
Liam: If anyone wants to pair on API wording ping me.
Maria: Thanks all — ping again in #eng-runtime when you have experiments. :memo:
